transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more. 

Um... I guess I came in because... well, my mind just doesn't seem to want to hold onto things lately. It's probably just me getting older, I'm sure it's nothing too serious. But, for instance, I help out with this youth maker program, and I'll sit down to write a simple note—something I used to be able to do in my sleep, really—and the numbers and words just sort of... scatter on me. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit that out loud, to be honest. Am I explaining that okay? Is that the sort of thing you need to know?
When did you first notice your mind having trouble holding onto things?

Oh, well... it hasn't been very long, really. Just about three weeks, I think. 

I almost hesitate to mention this, because I really don't want to sound like I'm making excuses or being overly dramatic... but, um, my older sister passed away right around then. I've just been a little out of sorts since it happened. I'm sure it's just a normal reaction to the stress of the funeral and everything, right? I mean, does that sound like a reasonable explanation to you?
Have you had trouble remembering things that happened before your sister passed away?

Oh, no, I don't believe so. Things from before... well, my memory of all that seems perfectly fine, really. I can remember past events just as well as I always could. 

It's just... just the day-to-day things right now that seem to get a bit muddy when I try to focus on them. I hope I'm being helpful by distinguishing that. Does that make sense to you? Is it a good sign that my older memories are still intact?
Have you had trouble learning new things since your sister passed away?

Oh, goodness... I don't think I've really tried to learn anything brand new lately, to be completely honest. Since she passed, I've mostly just been keeping to my usual routines—well, trying to, anyway. 

So I haven't really put myself in a position to notice if taking in completely new information is difficult right now. I'm sorry if that's not a very helpful answer. Is it okay if I'm just not sure about that one? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find that your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow when you're trying to think clearly?

Well, um... yes, I suppose so. I actually... well, I came in because my mind just really will not hold onto things anymore. I feel a bit foolish even admitting it, to be honest. 

Like, I'll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program I help out with—something I could absolutely do in my sleep before all this—and... I don't know, the numbers and words just seem to scatter on me. 

I'm sure it's just the grief and exhaustion catching up to me, wouldn't you say? I really don't want to make a big fuss over it if it's just a normal reaction. Does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about? Am I giving you the right sort of examples?
Do you find it difficult to stay on topic when talking to someone?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. Staying on topic seems to be okay. I try very hard to focus on what the other person is saying and just stick to that. 

I haven't been rambling or going off-track with you today, have I? I always want to make sure I'm answering your questions directly and not wasting your time. I think my conversations with others have been pretty normal in that regard, but please do let me know if I'm not being clear enough. Did I answer that one okay for you?
Do you ever feel disoriented or unsure about what's going on around you?

Oh, no, I don't think I've had anything quite like that. I mean, I know where I am and what day it is, things like that. 

I might be a little foggy sometimes, like I mentioned before with my thoughts scattering, but I'm definitely not lost or confused about my surroundings. I try very hard to keep my wits about me. 

I hope that's a good sign? I mean, it's normal to just feel a bit tired without being completely disoriented, right? I want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, but honestly, I think I'm doing okay in that department. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Do you have trouble paying attention to things?

Well, yes... I suppose that ties right into what I was saying a moment ago. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I don't want to take up your time with the same old complaints. 

But yes, paying attention is... it's just become so difficult. Like I mentioned with the youth maker program I volunteer for... I try to sit down and just focus on writing a simple note, and my mind just won't hold onto it. The words and numbers just scatter. It's terribly embarrassing, to be honest. I used to be so sharp with those things. 

I'm sure it's just a temporary blip, though. Just a bit of fatigue making it hard to concentrate, wouldn't you think? I really try my best to stay focused, I promise. Does that make sense? Am I explaining it right?
Have you noticed any trouble finding the right words when you're talking to someone?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, at my age, maybe a word slips my mind every great once in a while, just like anyone else, but nothing out of the ordinary. I feel like I can usually say exactly what I mean to say without too much fuss. 

I certainly hope I've been articulating myself well enough with you today? I try very hard to be clear so I'm not making your job more difficult or causing any confusion. I've been making sense so far, haven't I?
Have you had trouble recalling things that happened in the last few days?

Oh, no, I don't believe so. My memory for recent things seems to be... well, it's holding up just fine, thankfully. I can remember what I did yesterday, what I had for dinner, things of that nature. 

It's really just the focusing part that trips me up when I'm trying to do a task, but my actual memory of the last few days is perfectly intact. I try to make a point of keeping track of everything so I can give you accurate answers. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so I'm not making your job any harder than it needs to be.
Are you having trouble completing your daily tasks due to your mind wandering or having trouble focusing?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say it stops me from getting my daily things done. I mean, even with the little focus issues I mentioned before, I still make absolutely sure to finish my chores. I wouldn't want to just let things go and be a burden to anyone, you know? 

So... the laundry, the dishes, keeping the house tidy... I just push through and get them all finished. I might have to double-check myself sometimes, but I do complete them. I really try my hardest not to let it interfere with my day-to-day responsibilities. I hope that shows I'm putting in a good effort? I just want to make sure I'm handling things the right way.
Do you feel mentally foggy or like you're in a haze most of the time?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I feel foggy or hazy most of the time. I mean, maybe there's a moment here or there where I feel a little tired, but I try very hard to stay sharp and present. I wouldn't want to walk around in a daze all day. 

I make sure to keep my mind active, you know, reading the paper and such, so I'm not just sitting there staring at the wall. I think I've been pretty clear-headed today, wouldn't you say? I certainly hope I haven't seemed confused or out of it during our talk. I really do want to give you the best answers I can.
Have you been having trouble making decisions lately?

Well... decisions... I try not to make a fuss about it, but I suppose I have been a little slower there. Actually, that's sort of the main reason I finally came in to see someone. I hope it's alright to admit this, but my mind just... it really will not hold onto things anymore. 

I'll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program I help with—something I used to be able to do in my sleep, you know? But now, the numbers and the words, they just sort of scatter on me when I'm trying to put it all together and figure out what to do. I'm really trying my absolute best to push through it, though, and not let it cause any problems. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be as accurate as I can for you.
Do you find it hard to concentrate on tasks for a long period of time?

Well... yes, I suppose that ties into what I was just saying. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but... yes, holding onto a task for a while has gotten quite difficult. 

Like I mentioned with those notes for the youth program... I'll sit there, trying so hard to concentrate and get it done right. But after a little bit, it's just like the words and the numbers won't stay put in my head. They just scatter. I used to be able to focus on those things for hours if I needed to, without a second thought. Now... I just can't seem to keep my attention on it for very long, no matter how much effort I put in. I feel terrible about it, honestly. I'm really trying not to let anyone down. Does that answer what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find yourself getting easily distracted by things around you?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm easily distracted by things around me, like a bird out the window or a noise in the hall. I try very hard to pay attention to what's in front of me. It's more... well, like I was saying before, it's the task itself that slips away from me. 

I'll be sitting there, trying to write those notes for the youth maker program, and there won't be a single distraction in the room. But my mind just... it just won't hold onto the numbers and words anymore. They just scatter on me, all on their own. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I am still trying my best to get it done. I just... I used to do it in my sleep, and now I can't seem to hold the pieces together in my head. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I don't mean to keep bringing up the same example, I just want to be sure I'm explaining it right for you.
Have you been feeling anxious or overwhelmed by your difficulty with focusing and completing tasks?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I feel anxious, exactly. I mean, I don't want to make a big fuss or sound like I'm complaining. I know everyone slows down a bit, and I'm really trying my best to just handle it quietly. 

I suppose... well, maybe "overwhelmed" is a little strong, but it does get a bit frustrating when I can't do the things I used to do so easily. But I really try not to let it get to me too much, you know? I just keep pushing through, hoping it'll get better if I just try harder. I don't want to be a bother to anyone with it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question properly.
Do you have trouble finding the right words when you're trying to express a thought or idea?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any trouble with finding words, no. I mean, sometimes I might pause for a second, just like anyone my age might, but... I can still explain what I'm thinking just fine. 

I really try to make sure I'm clear when I talk to people, especially here with you. I don't want to give the wrong impression or make things confusing. As long as I'm making sense to you now, I think my words are coming out okay. Am I explaining things alright for you so far? I just want to be sure I'm being helpful.
Do you feel like your difficulty focusing is impacting your mood?

Well, um... I suppose it might be, a little bit. I don't want to sound ungrateful, because I know I have a good life and a wonderful wife, but... well, most days lately, I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. 

I try my hardest not to let it show, especially around her. She talks so kindly to me, trying to cheer me up, but... I just feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of a well, looking up. It's so hard to explain without sounding like I'm just feeling sorry for myself. I really don't want to be a burden or bring anyone else down. I'm trying to stay positive, I really am. Do you think that's normal, feeling that way? I hope I'm not overstating things, I just want to give you the right picture.
Do you think your trouble focusing is related to your feelings of sadness or the heavy, hollow feeling you mentioned?

Well, um... I really don't know for sure. I haven't really thought about them being connected like that. I mean, I suppose they could be? 

I just... I don't want to make it sound like everything is falling apart or anything. I just try to take each day as it comes and do the best I can with what I have. I'm sorry, I'm not sure if that's the kind of answer you're looking for. I just wouldn't want to guess and tell you the wrong thing. Is it okay that I'm not really sure about that?
Do you find that external stimuli, such as noise or other people talking, distract you from your tasks?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, my wife has the television on sometimes, or the neighbors might be out in their yard, but I don't really let it bother me. I try to just tune it out and keep to myself, you know? 

I really wouldn't say I'm easily distracted by those things. I try to be very considerate and not let normal everyday noises upset me. Everyone has a right to go about their day, after all. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm irritable or complaining about the people around me. I really try to be patient with things like that.

patient.answer:

I really try to make sure I'm clear when I talk to people, especially here with you. I don't want to give the wrong impression or make things confusing. target_item.name: Depressed_Mood

patient.answer:
Well, um... I suppose it might be, a little bit. I don't want to sound ungrateful, because I know I have a good life and a wonderful wife, but... well, most days lately, I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. 

I try my hardest not to let it show, especially around her. She talks so kindly to me, trying to cheer me up, but... I just feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of a well, looking up. It's so hard to explain without sounding like I'm just feeling sorry for myself. I really don't want to be a burden or bring anyone else down. I'm trying to stay positive, I really am. Do you think that's normal, feeling that way? I hope I'm not overstating things, I just want to give you the right picture.
